source: IranWatch, Wikipedia, CSIS, Palestine Chronicle, EurAsian Times, CNN

iranianOffensive.name: Shahab-3
iranianOffensive.notes: Based on North Korean technology. Backbone of Iran's ballistic force for 20+ years. Inaccurate but heavy warhead.

iranianOffensive.name: Ghadr-1
iranianOffensive.notes: Extended-range Shahab-3 variant. Improved guidance. Smaller warhead enables greater range.

iranianOffensive.name: Emad
iranianOffensive.notes: Precision-guided Shahab-3 variant with maneuverable reentry vehicle (MaRV). Significant accuracy upgrade over base Shahab-3.

iranianOffensive.name: Sejjil-2
iranianOffensive.notes: Two-stage solid fuel. 'Dancing missile' — erratic trajectory designed to evade interceptors. Fastest conventional missile in Iranian arsenal.

iranianOffensive.name: Kheibar Shekan
iranianOffensive.notes: 3rd-gen IRGC missile. Satellite-aided guidance. Maneuverable warhead (MaRV). Among most accurate in Iranian arsenal.

iranianOffensive.name: Khorramshahr-4 (Kheibar)
iranianOffensive.notes: Heaviest warhead in Iranian arsenal (1,500 kg). Range extends to 3,000+ km with lighter payload. Cluster variant carries 80 submunitions.

iranianOffensive.name: Fattah-1
iranianOffensive.notes: Iran's first hypersonic-class missile. Terminal maneuvering reentry vehicle (MaRV) designed specifically to defeat Arrow-3 and THAAD.

iranianOffensive.name: Haj Qasem
iranianOffensive.notes: Named after Qassem Soleimani. Solid fuel enables rapid launch. Road-mobile.

iranianOffensive.name: Shahed-136 / Geran-2
iranianOffensive.notes: Iranian-designed, mass-produced by Russia (Alabuga). The defining weapon of the drone age. Cheap enough to overwhelm air defenses through volume.

iranianOffensive.name: Shahed-238
iranianOffensive.notes: Advanced jet-powered variant. Much faster than Shahed-136. Multiple guidance modes including anti-radiation seeker.

iranianOffensive.name: Soumar / Hoveyzeh
iranianOffensive.notes: Terrain-following flight at <50m altitude for radar evasion. Based on Russian Kh-55 design obtained from Ukraine.

iranianOffensive.name: Paveh
iranianOffensive.notes: Long-range cruise missile. Low-altitude flight profile.

airDefenseSystems.name: Iron Dome
airDefenseSystems.notes: Designed for Hamas rockets. Struggles against ballistic missiles and cluster warheads. Stocks running low.

airDefenseSystems.name: David's Sling
airDefenseSystems.targets: Tactical ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, aircraft, drones (40-300 km)
airDefenseSystems.intercept_rate: Variable — 2 failed intercepts near Dimona on Mar 21
airDefenseSystems.notes: Middle tier. Upgraded before current war. Two failed intercepts near Dimona nuclear reactor raised alarm.

airDefenseSystems.name: Arrow-2
airDefenseSystems.notes: Upper atmospheric intercept. Fragmentation warhead (not hit-to-kill). Being replaced by Arrow-3.

airDefenseSystems.name: Arrow-3
airDefenseSystems.intercept_rate: High — but Fattah-1 MaRV designed to defeat it
airDefenseSystems.notes: Hit-to-kill in space. Most advanced Israeli system. Production rate tripled since war began.

airDefenseSystems.name: THAAD
airDefenseSystems.intercept_rate: High — but radar destroyed by Iran in UAE
airDefenseSystems.status: DEGRADED — AN/TPY-2 radar destroyed in UAE
airDefenseSystems.notes: 48 interceptors per battery. AN/TPY-2 radar costs $600M each. Only 10 in the world. Iran destroyed one with a $10K drone.

airDefenseSystems.name: Patriot PAC-3
airDefenseSystems.targets: Aircraft, cruise missiles, tactical ballistic missiles
airDefenseSystems.intercept_rate: High against aircraft/cruise, moderate against ballistic
airDefenseSystems.notes: Workhorse of US air defense in the Gulf. Deployed at multiple bases. Each PAC-3 costs $4M vs $30K Shahed drone.

airDefenseSystems.name: Aegis / SM-3
airDefenseSystems.status: Operational — deployed on destroyers in Gulf
airDefenseSystems.notes: Most expensive interceptor in use. Successfully intercepted one of two Iranian ICBMs. $36M per shot.

airDefenseSystems.name: AN/FPS-132
airDefenseSystems.targets: Detection only — ballistic missiles and space objects
airDefenseSystems.notes: Costs $1.1 BILLION. Iran struck it with a $10,000 drone. Feeds tracking data to all missile defense systems. Only 10 worldwide.

usOffensive.name: B-1B Lancer
usOffensive.notes: Deployed from Diego Garcia. Flying over Tehran with air superiority. GPS and laser-guided munitions.

usOffensive.name: B-2 Spirit
usOffensive.status: Used in opening strikes — limited bunker buster supply
usOffensive.notes: Only platform that can deliver GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrators against deeply buried nuclear facilities. Only 20 exist.

usOffensive.name: Tomahawk (BGM-109)
usOffensive.notes: Launched from destroyers and submarines. Terrain-following. Used to suppress Iranian air defenses in opening wave.

usOffensive.name: ATACMS
usOffensive.notes: Army Tactical Missile System. Fired from HIMARS/MLRS launchers at Gulf bases.

usOffensive.name: PRISM (Precision Strike Missile)
usOffensive.notes: ATACMS replacement. Longer range. Used alongside Tomahawks in opening strikes.

data.note: vs Shahed = 130:1 ratio in Iran's favor
Only 10 in world. Destroyed by $10K drone (60,000:1)
